title: Sum of the Border

concept.title: Which cells are on the border
body: A cell is on the border of an `n` by `m` matrix when it is in the first or last row, or in the first or last column. In code that is a four-part condition on the two indexes.

body.code:
if i == 0 or i == n - 1 or j == 0 or j == m - 1:
    total += g[i][j]

body: Because the test is one `or`, a corner cell (for example `i == 0` and `j == 0`) is still added only once. A matrix with one row or one column is all border.

statement: Given a matrix with `n` rows and `m` columns, print the sum of all cells on its border. Every cell is counted once.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `m` integers each.
hints: Loop over all cells and decide for each whether it is on the border.
A border cell has `i == 0`, `i == n - 1`, `j == 0` or `j == m - 1`.
Join the four tests with `or`, so no cell is added twice.

starter.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
